reasoning: No proposals, so no trades. I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (0.55): SPY is 1.62% under its 200-day and the regime filter is off. That leaves TLT and GLD as the only allowed buys, with BND and IEF wash-sale blocked. GLD is on his avoid list (5d -7.67%). TLT is at its target weight of about 8% of equity, the cap on that sleeve (L4), and the only fresh evidence for adding is a hedge week the 11-23 and 11-24 adds already counted. About 49.6% cash sits idle because of the regime filter, not by choice, and that cash is not a reason to keep any invalidated position. None is invalidated. Re-entry plan, as the Skeptic asked: when the filter turns on, deploy toward about 75-80% invested within a week. Put the money first into menu names in the Market Analyst's favored sectors that each carry their own stop (L9), at about 3-5% each, not into the KR/SAM Staples bucket and not into a single shared-stop index pair. Then add a broad US ETF sized as one position once its wash-sale block ends. L7 review: there are no stop_alerts and every stop block reads ok, with SAM closest at 5.33% above $201. TLT's clauses are unmet: SPY 5d is -1.86% against TLT 5d +2.44%, and TLT is 1.34% under its 200-day, inside the 4% test. KR's cyber clause is unconfirmed and its guidance clause is untested until the 12-03 call. SAM has no guidance-cut 8-K and is still on the menu. DPZ is on the menu with CFO above net income and no guidance cut. CARG, IDXX, INCY, MSCI and VRSN have no guidance cut, reversal or negative 8-K. Earnings dates come from the News Analyst's filings check (L2). Under L10, all live clauses are relative or event-based. TLT plan for the 12-09 FOMC: hold through it unless a clause trips, with no adds. The stop is restated from the $81.10 blended cost (L6). I disagree with three holdings-review reasons, though not with the verdicts. (1) KR and SAM: the Proposer leans on negative beta, which both stored theses call an artifact. The holds rest on the favored Staples tilt and cash backing instead. On KR I weighed the Skeptic's one-third pre-print trim. I would not have approved a trim at 6% of equity: that is half the weight WMT had when we trimmed it before its print, so a 10% gap costs about 0.6% of equity, and Staples still leads (XLP 21d +4.46% vs SPY -6.09%). Under L8 I name it the first equity sell candidate, and the Proposer owes a sell proposal or a hold verdict at the next run that does not rest on beta.
